checks: A rank-d matrix with d+1 columns has one-dimensional kernel, spanned here by a vector all of whose entries are positive. Hence no continuous normal is zero, since that would supply a kernel coordinate vector. An interior B point consequently has strictly negative margin in each row, so their positive combination gives D<0.

The specified positive row factors make the normal sum zero and the base-coefficient sum −(d+1). The normal evaluation map has rank d and image in the d-dimensional sum-zero subspace. The target vector (−1−tᵢ) has zero sum, so one unique q solves all equations.

Substitution x−y=x′+qz makes each base coefficient −1. Translation on each fiber preserves volume and midpoint compatibility, and the cap-normal change is invertible with the shear fixed. At base 1, absence of positive captured volume implies B lies in all weak halfspaces vᵢ·x′≤1, by density of its interior.

The displayed barycentric affine map is one-to-one by rank and onto the coordinate-sum-one plane by dimension. Nonnegative barycentric coordinates are exactly the constraints of the enclosing simplex. The origin maps to the centroid.

On the rows with an interior mark, proper A capture, and fixed-mark local minimality, the transformed cap meets every hypothesis of the proper/zero row lemma. Its section areas and the midpoint inclusion follow with levels −1,0,1. The purely affine normalization requires no minimizing hypothesis.

dependencies.hypotheses: For each conditional row use its one-mark proper/zero hypothesis after shear: A is proper, K contains the interior translated mark, B captures zero, local minimality is preserved, and the compatible fiber midpoint condition is unchanged. This yields the area and midpoint conclusions.

overlap.comparison: It uses a distinct-mark shear to make the base coefficient vanish in the displacement direction of two maximizing bases. The present same-mark circuit with a common zero endpoint gives the common coefficient −1 and a bounded enclosing simplex.
It yields a minimal positive critical circuit and covers a fiber plane, but does not give the strict common-endpoint sign, normalized coefficients or enclosing simplex.

summary: The positive circuit gives a strictly negative weighted base coefficient, a simultaneous shear normalization, and one enclosing simplex for the common zero endpoint.
